title: All-hands March 2026 - announcement + Q&A (scratchpad)
content:
Draft for all-hands announcement + Q&A.

Context / purpose:
- Quick update to company on product milestones (hosted API improvements + Dedicated capacity launch), hiring/OKR progress, and a short roadmap signal.
- Keep it upbeat and concise - ~8-10 min talk from CEO + 5-7 min for top-level Q&A. Detailed follow-up doc + Confluence links after the meeting.

Top-line announcement (opening paragraph, for CEO):
- Thanks + recognition for shipping throughput and reliability improvements.
- Announce: Redwood Dedicated pilot expanded to 3 more customers; early metrics show 20-30% latency improvement on p99 for our standard configs vs last quarter.
- Announce: Hosted API price adjustments for high-volume customers (pilot) + new Optimize recommendations UI in console (beta).
- Emphasize: Our thesis - serving-first approach - and how these launches reduce customer TCO and improve predictability for production apps.

Talking points (bullet form, for CEO/Head of Product):
- What shipped since last all-hands (concise):
  - Serving runtime: KV cache improvements + continuous batching tweaks - net p50/p95 gains across most seq-lengths.
  - Dedicated: expanded pilot, case studies in progress (1 enterprise + 2 mid-market).
  - Console: Optimize tab beta + token-level cost heatmap.
  - Private: early on-prem integration completed with customer X (NDA) - lessons learned about KMS integration.

- Why it matters:
  - Customers get more predictable latency and lower unit cost - fewer surprise infra bills.
  - This is our moat: unify runtime + routing + observability so engineering teams can ship faster without owning infra.

- Roadmap signal (high level):
  - Next 90 days: GA of Optimize recommendations + official Dedicated pricing tiers + improved dev experience for function/tool calling.
  - 6-12 months: deeper private deployment automation, expanded region coverage, better model variant routing.

Anticipated Q&A (prep answers)
1) Q: Any customer-visible downtime or incidents we should call out?
   A: No customer-impacting incidents since last all-hands. We did have a degraded deploy window on 2026-02-12 (internal postmortem exists) - root cause was failing kernel selection logic on a narrow model family; mitigations are in place (fallback path + additional test cases).

2) Q: Pricing changes - will existing customers be grandfathered?
   A: Pilot pricing changes are opt-in for now. We will communicate 60-day notice for any mandatory changes and offer migration help. Dedicated contracts separate - customers on committed terms unaffected unless they choose to upgrade.

3) Q: How are we measuring Optimize beta success?
   A: Primary metrics: % of recommendations accepted, delta in per-token cost for customers who accept, and maintain model output quality (we track eval regressions tied to prompt sets). Targets: 25% acceptance and 10-15% cost reduction for pilot cohort.

4) Q: Hiring - which roles are highest priority?
   A: Infra SRE (2), Serving runtime engineers (3), Solutions eng for Dedicated (2), and a Senior Product Manager for Optimize. Recruiting update: active on-campus and a targeted agency for SRE roles.

5) Q: Are we still prioritizing open-source model support?
   A: Yes - we plan to add 3 more open model variants to the catalog next quarter with vetted performance profiles; the goal is to give customers easier drop-in replacements to trade cost vs quality.

Open items / notes-to-self (stuff to fix in final doc):
- Insert link to Dedicated pilot case study (Confluence) - currently waiting legal sign-off.
- Finalize wording on pricing pilot (Emily to approve).
- Add one slide with p99 latency chart (Ops to supply numbers by 2026-03-03).
- Pull a short customer quote (Sarah from CS) for one-liner.

Communication plan (post all-hands):
- Publish full announcement + FAQ to #company-updates Slack + Confluence page with deeper links (within 24 hours).
- Email digest to customers impacted by Dedicated pilot + account exec outreach.
- Blog post with technical deep-dive on Optimize (target March 30).

Style notes (voice):
- Keep it engineering-forward, but avoid too much jargon in the all-hands.
- Use concrete numbers where available; otherwise signal intent clearly.

Draft Q&A to paste into Confluence FAQ (short answers):
- Will this change my API? No. Hosted API surface stays the same; pricing & routing improvements are behind-the-scenes.
- How do I join the Dedicated pilot? Customer success will reach out; internal form (link) for referrals.
- What if Optimize suggestions change model outputs? We require acceptance and run A/B checks; recommendations include quality metrics and rollbacks.

Slack/links to include in final doc (placeholders):
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Optimize-Beta
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-524 (Optimize acceptance metrics)

Rough slide order (for final deck):
1) Title + TL;DR (30s)
2) What shipped last quarter (60s)
3) Dedicated pilot update + p99 chart (90s)
4) Optimize beta + console screenshots (60s)
5) Roadmap signal (45s)
6) Hiring + shoutouts (30s)
7) Q&A (5-7 min)

Random notes / scratch ideas to maybe include:
- Short customer video / soundbite if CS can capture quick 10-15s comment.
- One-liner: "Serving is the hardest part of building fast, reliable LLM features - we're making it predictable."
- Consider a quick demo of Optimize recommendations live in the console (risky for the all-hands - lean toward screen recording).

End of scratchpad.
